findings.issue_text: P2: In thread mode, hang detection never stops the hung thread because the kill path is guarded by isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process), but a replacement thread is still created over the same shards, causing both threads to flush the same Redis shards and produce duplicate segments via produce_to_pipe

P2: In thread mode, the old and replacement threads share the same process_healthy_since / process_backpressure_since Value objects, so a slow-but-alive old thread keeps updating healthy_since, masking the replacement thread's health and preventing future restarts
P2: Replacing an uncaught AttributeError on Thread.kill() with silent data duplication turns a loud failure into silent duplicate segment production

P2: In join(), once the deadline expires, the break statement skips terminate() for the current and all remaining processes, so hung child processes are never terminated (old code unconditionally terminated after the wait loop)

P2: Hung flusher processes that survive past stopped=True can orphan and keep producing for the same shards during arroyo strategy teardown/replacement (e.g., rebalance), causing duplicate Kafka production alongside the new strategy's flushers

P3: Metric tag inconsistency — spans.buffer.flusher.produce is tagged {"shard": shard_tag} while spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce is tagged {"shards": shard_tag}, silently breaking dashboards/alerts that aggregate or compare the two metrics by tag

P3: max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards) treats an explicitly-passed flusher_processes=0 as 'auto'; combined with empty assigned_shards at create_with_partitions time, this results in zero flusher processes being created, no flushing, and no alerts, whereas the old code always created exactly one process

P3: In test_basic, monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None) globally patches the time module, making the subsequent time.sleep(0.1) (intended to give flusher threads time to process after drift change) a no-op; the test passes only due to fast polling, a latent flakiness source

Restart of hung/dead flusher never terminates the old thread when handle is a threading.Thread (produce_to_pipe is not None path): _ensure_processes_alive() only kills multiprocessing.Process handles, so a hung thread stays alive while a new one is spawned, causing duplicate concurrent flushers on the same shards, duplicate Kafka payloads, and unbounded thread growth

Per-submit Redis work now scales linearly with flusher process count: submit() calls record_stored_segments() and get_memory_info() once per flusher process (each with its own SpansBuffer/Redis connection), making Redis round trips and submit latency proportional to flusher_processes rather than constant, adding measurable Redis load and delaying poll()

Zero assigned shards at construction means no flusher ever runs silently: num_processes is computed once from buffer.assigned_shards in __init__; if empty at creation time, processes list is empty and _ensure_processes_alive() is a no-op that never creates processes, leaving segments for those shards unflushed in Redis (aging out or accumulating and driving backpressure toward MessageRejected)

In join(), once the deadline is exhausted, the outer for loop breaks before calling process.terminate(), so if process #1 hangs and consumes the full deadline, processes #2..N are never terminated (unlike the old code which unconditionally terminated after the wait loop)

In join(), if self.next_step.join(timeout) consumes the full timeout, the loop breaks on the first iteration and no flusher process is waited on or terminated at all, leaking live child processes holding Redis connections and mid-flight Kafka producers on shutdown

Memory accounting / record_stored_segments now runs on freshly constructed SpansBuffer instances that never receive store() calls, so instance-local 'used' accounting may always be ~0, making the max-memory-percentage backpressure check in submit() dead code and allowing unbounded Redis growth without MessageRejected protection

In thread mode, _ensure_processes_alive() only calls kill() on multiprocessing.Process instances, so a hung thread is never stopped or joined while _create_process_for_shards() creates a replacement, causing unbounded thread accumulation, duplicate flushers polling the same shards, and leaked SpansBuffer instances (with Redis connections) per restart

The --flusher-processes option has no validation (bare type=int, no IntRange(min=1)): passing 0 falls back to unbounded process count (one per shard), and passing a negative value creates zero flusher processes, meaning no flusher runs, _ensure_processes_alive() never fires, and spans silently accumulate in Redis
Empty assigned_shards at construction yields num_processes = 0, producing a silent no-op flusher where data is never flushed and no health signal or alert fires

New test_flusher_processes_limit only asserts internal state (len(flusher.processes), max_processes, shard counts) and never verifies actual sharded flushing behavior - no messages produced, no commits advanced, no check that spans written for shard N are flushed by the process owning shard N

test_basic adds time.sleep(0.1) to wait for flusher threads, but time.sleep is monkeypatched to a no-op, so the intended synchronization never happens and the test relies on scheduling luck, making it flaky

No test coverage for multi-process restart/unhealthy handling in _ensure_processes_alive - per-process health tracking, per-process restart counters, restarting only the affected process, and unhealthy metrics for all shards of a dead process are untested

join() no longer terminates hung processes (the old terminate() call was removed in the rewrite), so a hung flusher process will no longer be killed during consumer shutdown, and the shutdown-timeout path with multiple processes is untested

Edge cases of the new flusher_processes configuration are untested: flusher_processes=None, values larger than shard count (min() clamp), flusher_processes=0 silently falling back to one-process-per-shard, and the --flusher-processes click option wiring

Hung threads are never stopped on restart in the produce_to_pipe path; when a hang is detected the code skips kill() and spawns a new thread for the same shards while the old hung thread is still alive, causing two threads to poll the same shards in Redis concurrently, racing on get_flushed_segments and double-producing Kafka payloads with unbounded thread growth across restarts

Added time.sleep(0.1) in test_basic is a no-op because time.sleep was monkeypatched to a no-op lambda earlier in the test, so the flakiness 'fix' does nothing and the misleading comment masks a real race

Inconsistent defaults between factory and CLI: CLI option defaults to 1 but the factory's max_processes=None is coerced via 'or' to len(buffer.assigned_shards), silently changing other callers from 1 flusher process to N spawned processes; also 'max_processes or ...' conflates an explicit 0 with None

Dead code: _create_process_for_shard (singular) is defined but never invoked; the restart path calls _create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards) directly, leaving an unused O(n) reverse-lookup helper

Inconsistent metric tag keys: the same comma-joined shard string is tagged as {"shard": shard_tag} on spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes but as {"shards": shard_tag} on spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce, breaking dashboard/alert queries spanning these metrics

spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy is now incremented once per shard for the same single process failure instead of once per failure, silently changing the metric's semantics (N× inflation) without a name change

join() deadline break skips termination of all remaining processes: when timeout is consumed by next_step.join(timeout), remaining_time <= 0 triggers break before the wait/terminate block, leaving hung processes running past join() and relying solely on daemon=True for cleanup

SpawnProcess | Thread union leaks isinstance branching into every lifecycle method, forcing each call site to re-derive branch conditions with different capabilities (kill/terminate vs. nothing); a wrapper protocol like FlusherWorker with is_alive()/stop() would localize the divergence

Unvalidated `flusher_processes` CLI flag allows negative values (e.g. -1), causing `num_processes = -1`, empty process/shard maps, and the consumer running with zero flusher processes and zero health monitoring — leading to total silent flush failure and span data loss (P1)

`--flusher-processes 0` silently triggers the `or` fallback meaning 'one process per shard' rather than 0, a surprising and potentially resource-explosive interpretation (N spawn processes each with its own Kafka producer)

Thread-mode hang restart in `_ensure_processes_alive` creates a new thread for the same shards while the old hung thread remains alive, causing duplicate concurrent flushers racing on `buffer.flush()` and producing duplicate Kafka payloads / interleaved pipe writes if the old thread unblocks (P2)

Flusher no longer references the write-path buffer; it constructs fresh `SpansBuffer(shards)` instances per process and calls `record_stored_segments()` on never-written buffers, so any per-instance state consulted by `flush()` or metrics is silently empty (P2, needs verification against SpansBuffer internals)

Test's `time.sleep(0.1)` synchronization sleep is a no-op because `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)` patches it globally, so the flusher-loop ordering the test claims to stabilize is unverified and potentially flaky (P3)

Inconsistent metric tag key: `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` uses `tags={"shards": shard_tag}` while related metrics use `tags={"shard": shard_tag}`, breaking dashboards/alerts grouped by `shard` (P3)

`join()` skips termination of remaining processes when the deadline expires (`if remaining_time <= 0: break` exits the loop), so a spawn child blocked mid-produce can outlive `join()` and complete a produce after shutdown was declared (P3)

Tests only verify structure (`len(flusher.processes) == 2`, shard-count sum) and never verify that segments written to a shard are actually flushed by the process that owns it, leaving the multi-process flush path with zero end-to-end coverage (P3)

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: In thread mode, hang detection never stops the hung thread because the kill path is guarded by isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process), but a replacement thread is still created over the same shards, causing both threads to flush the same Redis shards and produce duplicate segments via produce_to_pipe

adjudication.rationale: In thread mode (`produce_to_pipe is not None`), `_create_process_for_shards` creates a `threading.Thread` running `SpanFlusher.main(...)`. In `_ensure_processes_alive`, when a thread is deemed unhealthy (dead or `hang` via `process_healthy_since[...]`), the restart path only attempts `process.kill()` when `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`, so a hung thread is not stopped. The code then unconditionally calls `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`, creating a new thread for the same shard list while the old thread can still be running. Because each thread has a `SpansBuffer(shards)` for the same shards, both can flush/produce for the same Redis shards, risking duplicate production via `produce_to_pipe`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: In thread mode, the old and replacement threads share the same process_healthy_since / process_backpressure_since Value objects, so a slow-but-alive old thread keeps updating healthy_since, masking the replacement thread's health and preventing future restarts

adjudication.rationale: In thread mode (`produce_to_pipe is not None`), `_create_process_for_shards` uses `threading.Thread` and cannot stop/kill the previous thread on restart (the kill branch is only for `multiprocessing.Process`). On restart it reuses the same `mp_context.Value` objects (`self.process_healthy_since[process_index]` / `self.process_backpressure_since[process_index]`) and passes them into the new thread as well. If the old thread is still alive and continues (or later resumes) updating `healthy_since.value` in `main` (`healthy_since.value = system_now`), it can mask the health of the replacement thread and interfere with future restart/backpressure detection. The old thread is also no longer tracked once `self.processes[process_index]` is overwritten.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Replacing an uncaught AttributeError on Thread.kill() with silent data duplication turns a loud failure into silent duplicate segment production

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive`, when a worker is a `threading.Thread` (used when `produce_to_pipe` is not `None`), the new code no longer errors on `kill()`; it conditionally kills only `multiprocessing.Process` instances and otherwise proceeds to `_create_process_for_shards(...)` (restart) without stopping the existing thread. If the thread is deemed unhealthy due to the hang check (`time.time() - process_healthy_since[...] > max_unhealthy_seconds`) but is still alive, this will start an additional thread handling the same shards while the old thread may continue running, which can lead to duplicate segment production. Previously, calling `self.process.kill()` on a thread would raise an uncaught `AttributeError` (loud failure) rather than silently running multiple flushers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: In join(), once the deadline expires, the break statement skips terminate() for the current and all remaining processes, so hung child processes are never terminated (old code unconditionally terminated after the wait loop)

P2: Hung flusher processes that survive past stopped=True can orphan and keep producing for the same shards during arroyo strategy teardown/replacement (e.g., rebalance), causing duplicate Kafka production alongside the new strategy's flushers
matched_golden_ids: Because flusher processes are created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, they are instances of multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess, which on POSIX is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process, so this isinstance check will always be false and hung processes won't be killed here.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that hung flusher processes can survive teardown/replacement and continue producing (orphaned flushers), leading to duplicates. This aligns with the golden issue’s core problem: the code fails to detect/kill hung flusher processes (due to the incorrect isinstance check on SpawnProcess), allowing them to persist.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Metric tag inconsistency — spans.buffer.flusher.produce is tagged {"shard": shard_tag} while spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce is tagged {"shards": shard_tag}, silently breaking dashboards/alerts that aggregate or compare the two metrics by tag

P3: max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards) treats an explicitly-passed flusher_processes=0 as 'auto'; combined with empty assigned_shards at create_with_partitions time, this results in zero flusher processes being created, no flushing, and no alerts, whereas the old code always created exactly one process

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` will treat an explicitly passed `max_processes=0` (from `flusher_processes`) as falsy and fall back to `len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, so the option value is not honored. Additionally, when `buffer.assigned_shards` is empty, this sets `self.max_processes` to `0`, leading to `self.num_processes = 0`, an empty `process_to_shards_map`, and `_create_processes()` creating no worker process/thread at all—whereas the previous implementation always created one via `_create_process()`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: In test_basic, monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None) globally patches the time module, making the subsequent time.sleep(0.1) (intended to give flusher threads time to process after drift change) a no-op; the test passes only due to fast polling, a latent flakiness source

Restart of hung/dead flusher never terminates the old thread when handle is a threading.Thread (produce_to_pipe is not None path): _ensure_processes_alive() only kills multiprocessing.Process handles, so a hung thread stays alive while a new one is spawned, causing duplicate concurrent flushers on the same shards, duplicate Kafka payloads, and unbounded thread growth

adjudication.rationale: In the `produce_to_pipe is not None` path, `_create_process_for_shards` uses `threading.Thread` (daemon) instead of a `multiprocessing.Process` (`make_process = threading.Thread`). In `_ensure_processes_alive`, when a thread is unhealthy/hung it will restart via `self._create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`, but it only attempts termination when `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`; for threads there is no stop/kill/join of the old thread. The old hung thread can therefore remain alive while a new thread for the same shard set is started, leading to concurrent duplicate flushers (duplicate produces) and potential unbounded thread accumulation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Per-submit Redis work now scales linearly with flusher process count: submit() calls record_stored_segments() and get_memory_info() once per flusher process (each with its own SpansBuffer/Redis connection), making Redis round trips and submit latency proportional to flusher_processes rather than constant, adding measurable Redis load and delaying poll()

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes SpanFlusher to create one SpansBuffer per flusher process (`shard_buffer = SpansBuffer(shards)` stored in `self.buffers`). In `submit()`, it now iterates `for buffer in self.buffers.values(): buffer.record_stored_segments()` and similarly aggregates memory info by iterating all buffers (`for buffer in self.buffers.values(): memory_infos.extend(buffer.get_memory_info())`). Previously these calls were made once on a single `self.buffer`. This makes per-`submit()` work O(num flusher processes). Whether each call implies Redis round trips isn’t shown in the diff, but the linear scaling behavior and added per-submit overhead are verifiable from the new loops.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Zero assigned shards at construction means no flusher ever runs silently: num_processes is computed once from buffer.assigned_shards in __init__; if empty at creation time, processes list is empty and _ensure_processes_alive() is a no-op that never creates processes, leaving segments for those shards unflushed in Redis (aging out or accumulating and driving backpressure toward MessageRejected)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that `SpanFlusher.__init__` derives `num_processes` from `len(buffer.assigned_shards)` and will create no processes/buffers when `assigned_shards` is empty (so `_ensure_processes_alive` becomes a no-op). However, the finding’s core claim—“leaving segments for those shards unflushed” because shards become assigned later to the same flusher instance—is not supported by the diff. There’s no evidence in the shown changes that `buffer.assigned_shards` is ever populated after construction without recreating the strategy/flusher, and if there are truly zero assigned shards, there may be nothing this consumer should flush anyway.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In join(), once the deadline is exhausted, the outer for loop breaks before calling process.terminate(), so if process #1 hangs and consumes the full deadline, processes #2..N are never terminated (unlike the old code which unconditionally terminated after the wait loop)

adjudication.rationale: In SpanFlusher.join(), the loop over `self.processes` breaks when `remaining_time <= 0` (deadline exhausted) before reaching later processes. Since `process.terminate()` is only called within the per-process loop body, processes after the one that consumed the full deadline will never be terminated, potentially leaving them running. This differs from the prior single-process logic that always reached the terminate call after the wait loop.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In join(), if self.next_step.join(timeout) consumes the full timeout, the loop breaks on the first iteration and no flusher process is waited on or terminated at all, leaking live child processes holding Redis connections and mid-flight Kafka producers on shutdown

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.join()`, a `deadline` is computed before `self.next_step.join(timeout)`, but `next_step.join` can consume the entire timeout. After that, the loop over `self.processes` checks `remaining_time` and `break`s immediately when `remaining_time <= 0`, which skips both the per-process wait loop and the subsequent `process.terminate()` call. This can leave flusher `multiprocessing.Process` instances running after shutdown (and thus holding resources like Redis connections / in-flight work).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Memory accounting / record_stored_segments now runs on freshly constructed SpansBuffer instances that never receive store() calls, so instance-local 'used' accounting may always be ~0, making the max-memory-percentage backpressure check in submit() dead code and allowing unbounded Redis growth without MessageRejected protection

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows SpanFlusher no longer keeps the original `buffer` (`self.buffer = buffer` removed) and instead constructs fresh `SpansBuffer(shards)` instances per process in `_create_process_for_shards`, then uses those new instances in `submit()` for `record_stored_segments()` and `get_memory_info()` aggregation. If `SpansBuffer`’s stored-segment/memory accounting depends on instance-local state updated by `store()` on the original buffer instance, this refactor could decouple the accounting from the actual writer and weaken backpressure. However, the diff alone doesn’t show `SpansBuffer`’s implementation, so the claim that the check is now definitively “dead code”/allows unbounded growth can’t be strictly verified here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In thread mode, _ensure_processes_alive() only calls kill() on multiprocessing.Process instances, so a hung thread is never stopped or joined while _create_process_for_shards() creates a replacement, causing unbounded thread accumulation, duplicate flushers polling the same shards, and leaked SpansBuffer instances (with Redis connections) per restart

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shards`, when `produce_to_pipe` is not `None`, the flusher runs as a `threading.Thread` (not a `multiprocessing.Process`). In `_ensure_processes_alive`, on detecting a hang (`time.time() - self.process_healthy_since[...] > max_unhealthy_seconds`), it only attempts `process.kill()` if `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`, so a hung thread is not stopped. It then unconditionally calls `_create_process_for_shards(...)`, spawning a replacement thread and creating a new `SpansBuffer(shards)` while the old thread (with its old buffer/Redis connections) can keep running. This can accumulate threads, duplicate shard flushing, and leak buffers/resources on repeated restarts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The --flusher-processes option has no validation (bare type=int, no IntRange(min=1)): passing 0 falls back to unbounded process count (one per shard), and passing a negative value creates zero flusher processes, meaning no flusher runs, _ensure_processes_alive() never fires, and spans silently accumulate in Redis

adjudication.rationale: The new click option `--flusher-processes` is declared with `type=int` and no range validation. In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` means a user-passed `0` is treated as falsy and ignored (falls back to per-shard default), which is surprising and unvalidated. More seriously, a negative value is accepted and leads to broken initialization: `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(...))` becomes negative, producing an empty `process_to_shards_map` via `range(self.num_processes)`, then the subsequent shard assignment loop does `self.process_to_shards_map[process_index].append(...)` and will KeyError (since the map is empty). So the lack of validation can crash the consumer / prevent flushers from starting (though the finding’s “silently accumulate” claim isn’t what the diff implies).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Empty assigned_shards at construction yields num_processes = 0, producing a silent no-op flusher where data is never flushed and no health signal or alert fires

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))` can become 0 when `buffer.assigned_shards` is empty. That makes `process_to_shards_map` empty, `_create_processes()` starts nothing, and `self.processes/self.buffers/process_*` dicts stay empty. Later, `submit()` calls `_ensure_processes_alive()` (loops over no processes, emits no unhealthy metrics) and records no stored segments / memory info (loops over no buffers), so the flusher becomes a silent no-op with no health/backpressure signaling in that scenario.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New test_flusher_processes_limit only asserts internal state (len(flusher.processes), max_processes, shard counts) and never verifies actual sharded flushing behavior - no messages produced, no commits advanced, no check that spans written for shard N are flushed by the process owning shard N

adjudication.rationale: In `test_flusher_processes_limit` (added in `tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py`), the test only inspects internal attributes (`len(flusher.processes)`, `flusher.max_processes`, `flusher.num_processes`, and shard distribution via `process_to_shards_map`) and then calls `step.join()` without driving any flushing/producing behavior (no spans inserted, no `step.poll()` loop, no assertions on `messages` via `produce_to_pipe`, and no assertions on `commits`). Given the diff adds nontrivial sharded multiprocessing behavior in `SpanFlusher` (per-shard buffers/process mapping and per-shard metrics/tags), this test verifies configuration/mapping but not the functional outcome of sharded flushing, making the review finding a concrete, diff-grounded test completeness concern rather than a demonstrated defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: test_basic adds time.sleep(0.1) to wait for flusher threads, but time.sleep is monkeypatched to a no-op, so the intended synchronization never happens and the test relies on scheduling luck, making it flaky
matched_golden_ids: The test_basic function in test_consumer.py uses a monkeypatched time.sleep that returns immediately, but then calls time.sleep(0.1) expecting it to actually wait.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe that test_basic uses a monkeypatched time.sleep that returns immediately, yet later calls time.sleep(0.1) intending a real delay for synchronization, making the test flaky/unreliable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test coverage for multi-process restart/unhealthy handling in _ensure_processes_alive - per-process health tracking, per-process restart counters, restarting only the affected process, and unhealthy metrics for all shards of a dead process are untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces substantial new logic in `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive()` (per-process `process_healthy_since`, `process_backpressure_since`, `process_restarts`, killing/restarting only the affected process, and emitting unhealthy metrics for each shard in the failed process). The added/modified tests (`test_basic`, `test_flusher_processes_limit`, and the backpressure assertion in `test_flusher`) only cover process-count/shard distribution and backpressure presence, not the unhealthy/restart paths (e.g., dead process, hang via `healthy_since` exceeding `max-unhealthy-seconds`, restart counter behavior, or per-shard metrics emission). This is a specific, diff-grounded missing coverage for newly added nontrivial behavior, not a proven functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: join() no longer terminates hung processes (the old terminate() call was removed in the rewrite), so a hung flusher process will no longer be killed during consumer shutdown, and the shutdown-timeout path with multiple processes is untested

adjudication.rationale: The finding misreads the diff: `SpanFlusher.join()` still calls `terminate()` for each `multiprocessing.Process` it iterates over (new loop at end of `join`). So it’s not true that the terminate call was removed entirely. However, the rewritten multi-process `join()` has a new timeout behavior: if `deadline` is exceeded before reaching later entries in `self.processes`, the `for` loop `break`s and those remaining processes will not be waited on or terminated. That shutdown-timeout/multiple-processes path also isn’t covered by the added tests (they only assert process counts/mapping and basic join).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Edge cases of the new flusher_processes configuration are untested: flusher_processes=None, values larger than shard count (min() clamp), flusher_processes=0 silently falling back to one-process-per-shard, and the --flusher-processes click option wiring

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new configuration/wiring for `flusher_processes` (new click option in `src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py`, new factory arg in `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory`, and `SpanFlusher.__init__(..., max_processes)` with `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` and `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))`). Tests added cover only one case (`flusher_processes=2` with 4 shards in `test_flusher_processes_limit`). The edge behaviors mentioned are not covered: `None` default path, `> shard count` clamping via `min(...)`, `0` being treated as falsy and falling back to `len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, and there is no test validating the new `--flusher-processes` click option is correctly wired through to the strategy factory/flusher. This is a specific, diff-grounded test gap rather than a confirmed defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hung threads are never stopped on restart in the produce_to_pipe path; when a hang is detected the code skips kill() and spawns a new thread for the same shards while the old hung thread is still alive, causing two threads to poll the same shards in Redis concurrently, racing on get_flushed_segments and double-producing Kafka payloads with unbounded thread growth across restarts

adjudication.rationale: In the `produce_to_pipe` path, `_create_process_for_shards` uses `threading.Thread` (not a `multiprocessing.Process`). When `_ensure_processes_alive` detects a hang (`time.time() - process_healthy_since[...] > max_unhealthy_seconds`), it only attempts `kill()` if `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`, so threads are never stopped. It then immediately calls `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`, spawning a new thread for the same shard set while the old (hung but still alive) thread remains, meaning multiple threads can concurrently poll/flush the same Redis shards and potentially double-produce. Repeated hang detections can therefore accumulate threads until `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS` triggers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Added time.sleep(0.1) in test_basic is a no-op because time.sleep was monkeypatched to a no-op lambda earlier in the test, so the flakiness 'fix' does nothing and the misleading comment masks a real race

adjudication.rationale: In `test_basic`, `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)` is set near the start. The newly added `time.sleep(0.1)` later in the test therefore calls the monkeypatched no-op and does not actually wait, making the comment "Give flusher threads time" misleading and leaving the intended race/flakiness unaddressed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inconsistent defaults between factory and CLI: CLI option defaults to 1 but the factory's max_processes=None is coerced via 'or' to len(buffer.assigned_shards), silently changing other callers from 1 flusher process to N spawned processes; also 'max_processes or ...' conflates an explicit 0 with None

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `flusher_processes: int | None = None` on `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory` and passes it through to `SpanFlusher(max_processes=...)`, but `SpanFlusher.__init__` sets `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)`. This means that when callers do not provide `flusher_processes` (factory default `None`), the flusher now spawns `len(buffer.assigned_shards)` processes by default, whereas previously there was a single background process (`_create_process`). Separately, the CLI option defaults to `1`, so defaults are inconsistent across entrypoints. Also, using `or` conflates an explicit `0` with `None` (0 would be treated as “use all shards”), matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead code: _create_process_for_shard (singular) is defined but never invoked; the restart path calls _create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards) directly, leaving an unused O(n) reverse-lookup helper

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher` (`src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py`), the helper `def _create_process_for_shard(self, shard: int):` is added but there is no invocation shown in this diff. The actual restart logic in `_ensure_processes_alive` restarts via `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)` directly, so this singular reverse-lookup helper appears redundant/unused (at least within the modified file), making it dead/extra code rather than a correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inconsistent metric tag keys: the same comma-joined shard string is tagged as {"shard": shard_tag} on spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes but as {"shards": shard_tag} on spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce, breaking dashboard/alert queries spanning these metrics
matched_golden_ids: In the SpanFlusher flush loop, metric tags inconsistently use 'shard' (e.g., in spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes) and 'shards' (in spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce) for the same shard identifier value. This prevents correct metric aggregation across flush stages — dashboards and alerts filtering by tag 'shard' will miss data tagged as 'shards' and vice versa.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same inconsistency in metric tag keys ('shard' vs 'shards') across the SpanFlusher flush loop metrics and correctly notes it breaks aggregation/querying for dashboards/alerts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy is now incremented once per shard for the same single process failure instead of once per failure, silently changing the metric's semantics (N× inflation) without a name change

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive`, when a process is unhealthy it now loops over `shards = self.process_to_shards_map[process_index]` and calls `metrics.incr("spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy", ...)` once per shard (`for shard in shards:`), adding a `shard` tag. Previously it incremented the metric exactly once per unhealthy event/process. This diff therefore verifiably changes the metric’s counting semantics (potential N× increase for multi-shard processes) without changing the metric name, which is an observability/monitoring compatibility concern rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: join() deadline break skips termination of all remaining processes: when timeout is consumed by next_step.join(timeout), remaining_time <= 0 triggers break before the wait/terminate block, leaving hung processes running past join() and relying solely on daemon=True for cleanup

adjudication.rationale: In SpanFlusher.join(), a global deadline is computed before `self.next_step.join(timeout)`. If `next_step.join(timeout)` consumes the timeout (or more), then in the subsequent loop over `self.processes`, the check `remaining_time = deadline - time.time(); if remaining_time <= 0: break` exits the loop before reaching the per-process `while process.is_alive()` wait and the `process.terminate()` call. This can leave some flusher processes/threads still running after `join()` returns, effectively relying on `daemon=True` for cleanup rather than enforcing termination.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SpawnProcess | Thread union leaks isinstance branching into every lifecycle method, forcing each call site to re-derive branch conditions with different capabilities (kill/terminate vs. nothing); a wrapper protocol like FlusherWorker with is_alive()/stop() would localize the divergence

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `self.processes: dict[int, SpawnProcess | threading.Thread]` (in `SpanFlusher.__init__`), and lifecycle methods must repeatedly branch on the concrete type to access process-only controls: `_ensure_processes_alive` does `if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process): process.kill()`, and `join` does `if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process): process.terminate()`. This matches the finding’s point that the Process-vs-Thread divergence is spread across methods rather than localized behind a single worker abstraction/protocol. It’s an architectural/maintainability concern, not a directly verifiable correctness defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unvalidated `flusher_processes` CLI flag allows negative values (e.g. -1), causing `num_processes = -1`, empty process/shard maps, and the consumer running with zero flusher processes and zero health monitoring — leading to total silent flush failure and span data loss (P1)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a `--flusher-processes` CLI option as `type=int` with no lower-bound validation, and wires it through `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory(... flusher_processes=...)` into `SpanFlusher(max_processes=...)`. In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` will keep negative values (e.g. -1) because they are truthy, then `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(...))` becomes negative. This makes `range(self.num_processes)` empty and then the shard distribution loop does `process_index = i % self.num_processes` and attempts `self.process_to_shards_map[process_index].append(...)`, which will error due to the empty map / invalid indices. So negative CLI values can break flusher process setup (crash/misbehavior). The finding’s “silent zero-process flush failure” is not strictly shown (it more likely errors), but the lack of validation is a real defect introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `--flusher-processes 0` silently triggers the `or` fallback meaning 'one process per shard' rather than 0, a surprising and potentially resource-explosive interpretation (N spawn processes each with its own Kafka producer)

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, the new argument is applied as `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` (flusher.py). If the CLI passes `--flusher-processes 0` (allowed by `click.Option(..., type=int)` with no validation), `0` is falsy and will fall back to `len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, i.e., “one process per shard”, which contradicts the user-supplied 0 and can unexpectedly spawn many processes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Thread-mode hang restart in `_ensure_processes_alive` creates a new thread for the same shards while the old hung thread remains alive, causing duplicate concurrent flushers racing on `buffer.flush()` and producing duplicate Kafka payloads / interleaved pipe writes if the old thread unblocks (P2)

adjudication.rationale: In thread-mode (`produce_to_pipe is not None`), `_create_process_for_shards` uses `threading.Thread` and stores it in `self.processes`. In `_ensure_processes_alive`, a restart is triggered not only when `not process.is_alive()` but also when the thread is still alive yet considered hung (`time.time() - self.process_healthy_since[...] > max_unhealthy_seconds`). On restart, the code only calls `process.kill()` when `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`; threads are not stopped/terminated, and `stopped` is not set. It then unconditionally calls `_create_process_for_shards(...)`, starting a new thread for the same `shards` while the old “hung” thread remains alive. This can lead to multiple concurrent flushers for the same shards (duplicate/interleaved `buffer.flush()` / `produce_to_pipe` activity) if the old thread resumes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Flusher no longer references the write-path buffer; it constructs fresh `SpansBuffer(shards)` instances per process and calls `record_stored_segments()` on never-written buffers, so any per-instance state consulted by `flush()` or metrics is silently empty (P2, needs verification against SpansBuffer internals)

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes SpanFlusher to stop storing/using the original `buffer` instance (it removes `self.buffer = buffer`) and instead creates new per-process `SpansBuffer(shards)` instances (`shard_buffer = SpansBuffer(shards)`), then calls `record_stored_segments()` on these new instances in `submit()` (`for buffer in self.buffers.values(): buffer.record_stored_segments()`). Whether this is actually incorrect depends on `SpansBuffer` internals (e.g., whether `flush()`, `record_stored_segments()`, or metrics rely on per-instance state set on the write-path buffer vs being purely Redis-backed/stateless). That cannot be verified from the diff alone, but it is a concrete, diff-grounded correctness/architecture concern worth reviewing against `SpansBuffer` behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test's `time.sleep(0.1)` synchronization sleep is a no-op because `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)` patches it globally, so the flusher-loop ordering the test claims to stabilize is unverified and potentially flaky (P3)
matched_golden_ids: Sleep in test_consumer.py won’t actually wait because time.sleep was monkeypatched above; consider restoring sleep or using a different sync to ensure the flusher has time to process.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that `time.sleep(0.1)` is ineffective because `time.sleep` was monkeypatched to a no-op, making the intended synchronization/flusher timing unverified and potentially flaky—same underlying issue as the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inconsistent metric tag key: `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` uses `tags={"shards": shard_tag}` while related metrics use `tags={"shard": shard_tag}`, breaking dashboards/alerts grouped by `shard` (P3)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows inconsistent metric tag keys: `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})` and `metrics.timing("spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes", ..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})` use `shard`, but `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})` uses `shards`. This is a real observability inconsistency introduced by the change and can break dashboard/alert grouping that expects `shard`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `join()` skips termination of remaining processes when the deadline expires (`if remaining_time <= 0: break` exits the loop), so a spawn child blocked mid-produce can outlive `join()` and complete a produce after shutdown was declared (P3)
matched_golden_ids: Breaking out of the loop when the deadline has elapsed can skip terminating remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown; consider ensuring termination is attempted even if the deadline is exceeded.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that the loop breaks when remaining_time <= 0, which skips handling/terminating the remaining processes, allowing a child process to outlive shutdown—same underlying issue as the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Tests only verify structure (`len(flusher.processes) == 2`, shard-count sum) and never verify that segments written to a shard are actually flushed by the process that owns it, leaving the multi-process flush path with zero end-to-end coverage (P3)

adjudication.rationale: The new test `test_flusher_processes_limit` only asserts structural properties of the new multi-(thread/process) flusher implementation (e.g. `len(flusher.processes) == 2`, `num_processes == 2`, and that shard counts sum to 4). It does not exercise the new shard-to-process buffer split introduced in `SpanFlusher.__init__` / `_create_process_for_shards` (creating per-process `SpansBuffer(shards)` and storing them in `self.buffers`) by writing segments for specific shards and asserting they are flushed/produced. Existing tests shown still mainly cover single-threaded behavior or backpressure state, so the newly added multi-shard distribution path lacks end-to-end verification of actual flushing/producing per assigned shard.
